name: Kawi (Old Javanese)

ancestors.notes: Sanskrit adstrate: retroflex/aspirate loan series, literary vocabulary

notes: Skeleton. Kawi / Old Javanese, the literary Austronesian language of early Java, here in romanised transliteration (Zoetmulder). Heavy Sanskrit lexical adstrate accounts for the retroflex and aspirate series. The pepet ⟨ě⟩=/ə/ is encoded; length is not phonemic. Stress exemption: Old Javanese (Kawi) word prominence is not phonemic and is not marked in the Kawi script; the language's stress, where described, is predictable from syllable weight rather than recoverable purely from the orthography modeled here. Source: Zoetmulder, P. J. (1982), Old Javanese-English Dictionary, introduction on phonology.
